world.title: A divided vote for the UN’s human rights chief
world.description: The UN General Assembly recently voted to reappoint Volker Türk as High Commissioner for Human Rights, making him the first person to serve two terms since the post was created in 1993. The 144 votes in favour marked a clear victory for human rights. But the 10 votes against, including by the USA, along with 13 abstentions and 26 no-shows, demonstrate the fragility of a system that depends on states cooperating and providing funding. At a time when major powers are attacking the international system, states that voted in favour of Türk’s second term must give the UN’s human rights functions their political and financial support.
